approved: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Board of Management Functions) Bill 2025
Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would let boards of management for jointly managed Commonwealth reserves on Indigenous land keep making decisions after a management plan expires.
Decisions made during the gap would have to follow the most recent expired management plan until a new plan takes effect.
Management plans expire after 10 years, and the bill aims to prevent a gap in board decision-making when a replacement plan is not ready.
Allows boards to continue decision-making after a management plan expires.
Requires board decisions during the gap to be consistent with the most recent expired management plan.
Ensures Indigenous participation in reserve management continues without interruption.
Traditional Owners and boards of management for Kakadu, Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa, and Booderee National Parks.

Argued that the bill's proposed time limit on reviews of defence honours decisions would prevent recognition of historic acts of bravery, citing Teddy Sheean, Richard Norden and veterans of Long Tan; moved opposition amendments and urged the minister to withdraw the bill, after which the question was put and the amendments were considered.

Supported extending arrangements for boards managing Kakadu, Uluru-Kata Tjuta and Booderee national parks, while arguing that broader environmental law reform was overdue and should improve assessment, establish an independent regulator and protect land, water, air and Indigenous cultural heritage; moved an amendment on cultural heritage protections, which was negatived, and the bill passed its second reading.

Presented the Selection of Bills Committee's sixth report for 2025, recommending immediate referral of four bills to committees for inquiry and reporting by 21 October 2025, 23 October 2025, 24 October 2025 and 30 October 2025; amendments proposed further referrals and reporting dates, and the amended report was adopted.
